newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen up on Wall Street rise.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen up on Wall Street rise.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to continue gaining on Tuesday, riding on psychological support from the sharp rise in the Dow Jones industrial average overnight, brokers said.

Brokers said the rise on Wall Street on hopes that a balanced federal budget deal would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates later this month could prompt foreign buying in some blue chip counters.
"Even if foreign buying remains limited because of political reasons, sustained interest from local investors will also be an important factor," one broker with a Japanese firm said.

He said positive reports on several secondary counters such as Elang Realty, Bhuwanatala Indah and Duta Pertiwi including talk of joint ventures, possible bond issues and rights issues would keep sentiment buoyant.

Property firm PT Elang Realty, which announced a 1996 net loss of 4.99 billion rupiah, was likely to attract market attention on reports it had signed a joint-venture agreement with privately-owned retailer Gelael, brokers said.
Sentiment on blue chip Citra Marga is expected to be firm on news that an Indonesian rating agency has given a positive outlook on its toll road project in Surabaya.
On Monday, the Jakarta composite index closed 4.89 points higher at 652.79 points after touching a day low of 647.66 points.
Telkom and Indosat, both of which are also listed in New York, made modest gains following the Dow's rise, brokers said.
Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,600 rupiah with some 1.3 million shares traded, while Indosat rose 175 rupiah to 7,050 rupiah with some 200,000 shares changing hands.
"Telkom had been expected to touch 3,600 rupiah this week. Any further upside is likely to be limited now as I don't see any new fundamental changes affecting the firm," one broker said.
Small property firm Bhuwanatala rose 25 rupiah to 725 rupiah in active trading following reports that the firm was expected to list a subsidiary and to buy five property projects, brokers said.
The most active property firm Duta Pertiwi rose 75 rupiah to 1,025 rupiah with volume approaching five million shares due to speculative reasons, brokers said.

Timah fell 25 rupiah to 3,675 rupiah following weak sentiment on mining firms because of news that the fabled Busang gold field was a dud, brokers said. Indonesian firms involved in Busang are not listed.
Tin mining firm Tambang Timah fell 75 rupiah to close at 3,625 rupiah with around one million shares traded.
Brokers said news that the fabled Busang gold find was a dud had dampened sentiment on mining firms doing business in Indonesia. Indonesian firms in the Busang project are not listed.
